resources.string: Scans the screen to find targetable elements and perform tasks according to the specified rules.
Enable the agent to be able to scan screen contents and run automations

string-array.name: tutorial_intro_body
string-array.item: TapOk lets you automate taps and other actions in Android apps.
Follow this quick tutorial to learn how to set up your first automation.

string-array.name: tutorial_step1_body
string-array.item: TapOk requires a background service to scan the screen and run your automations.
Open Accessibility settings, find TapOk (it may be under \"Installed apps\" or \"Downloaded services\") and switch it on.
Once enabled, a floating button will appear on your screen. You\'ll use it in the next step.

string-array.name: tutorial_step2_body
string-array.item: To write an automation you need to know what screen elements TapOk can interact with. A screen scanner is provided to help with that.
Open the app you want to automate, then tap \"Scan screen\" on TapOk\'s floating button to capture a scan of the active window.

string-array.name: tutorial_step3_body
string-array.item: Open your recent scan from the floating button menu (\"Toggle button\" \> \"View scans\").
Elements that TapOk can interact with will be highlighted.

item.li: Tap an element (e.g. a button) to select it.
Tap \"Create rule from this element\" to start creating a rule for this element.

string-array.name: tutorial_step4_body
string-array.item: A rule creation form will open, pre-filled with data from your selected element.

item.li: Review the data: keep only the details needed to uniquely identify your target, removing unnecessary filters speeds up matching.
Choose an action: select what TapOk should do, e.g. click the element.

string-array.item: That\'s it! TapOk will now perform this action automatically whenever it sees an element matching your description.

string-array.name: accessibility_api_usage_disclosure
string-array.item: To automate your actions, TapOk uses the Accessibility API:

item.li: analyzes the active window\'s contents and identifies targetable elements,
performs clicks and gestures on your behalf according to rules you specify.

string-array.item: The data is processed within TapOk, locally on your device. It is not transmitted to external servers or third parties.

resources.string: Select a rule to edit, or create a new one
The rule\'s action runs on any UI element that matches all the following criteria.
One of these is used to find a matching element. If multiple are filled in, the topmost one is used for the search and the rest act as post-search filters.
After the search, these filters are applied. Only fill in when needed to distinguish between similar elements — additional filters slow down matching.

\"Package name\" of the window\'s top-level element — normally the owning app\'s package. Visible in the top bar when viewing a scan.

string-array.name: no_elements_in_scan
string-array.item: You can try again and scan something else. Note that when multiple windows are visible only the one you are interacting with is scanned.
